questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sufficient condition for guaranteeing triangle congruence?
questions.explanation: AAA guarantees that two triangles have the exact same shape (similarity), but it does not guarantee that they have the same size. For example, an equilateral triangle with side length 2 cm and another with side length 10 cm both have angles of 60°, but they are not congruent.

questions.question: If ΔHEN ≅ ΔBIG, then vertex H corresponds to vertex _____, and side EN corresponds to side _____.
questions.explanation: In congruence notation ΔHEN ≅ ΔBIG, the order of letters specifies exact vertex correspondence: H↔B, E↔I, N↔G. Therefore, side EN corresponds to side IG.

questions.question: True or False: Any two equilateral triangles are always congruent to each other.
questions.explanation: False. While all equilateral triangles have equal angles measuring 60° (satisfying AAA), their side lengths can differ. Congruence requires both identical shape and identical size.

questions.question: In an isosceles triangle ΔABC, side AB = AC and vertex angle ∠A = 40°. Calculate the measures of base angles ∠B and ∠C.
questions.explanation: In ΔABC, since AB = AC, the angles opposite to them are equal, so ∠B = ∠C. The sum of interior angles in a triangle is 180°. Therefore, ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180° ⇒ 40° + 2(∠B) = 180° ⇒ 2(∠B) = 140° ⇒ ∠B = 70° and ∠C = 70°.

questions.question: In quadrilateral ABCD, diagonal AC bisects ∠BAD and AB = AD. Prove that ΔABC ≅ ΔADC using a suitable congruence criterion.
questions.explanation: In ΔABC and ΔADC: 1) AB = AD (Given). 2) ∠BAC = ∠DAC (Since AC bisects ∠BAD). 3) AC = AC (Common side). By the SAS (Side-Angle-Side) criterion, two sides and the included angle of ΔABC equal two sides and the included angle of ΔADC, so ΔABC ≅ ΔADC.

questions.question: Explain why the SSA (Side-Side-Angle) condition is generally invalid for proving triangle congruence, and identify the special case where SSA does guarantee congruence.
questions.correct_answer: SSA allows two non-congruent triangles with same 2 sides and non-included angle; RHS is the special right-angled case.
questions.explanation: In general, given two sides and a non-included angle, a compass arc can intersect the third side at two distinct points, creating two non-congruent triangles (one acute and one obtuse). The special exception occurs in right-angled triangles where the non-included angle is 90°; here, by Pythagoras Theorem, the third side is fixed uniquely, establishing the RHS criterion.

questions.question: An engineer designs a bridge truss containing two triangular support frames ΔPQS and ΔRQS on opposite sides of a central vertical beam QS. Given that PQ = RQ = 15 m, ∠PQS = ∠RQS = 35°, and PS = 12 m. (a) Prove that ΔPQS ≅ ΔRQS. (b) Determine the exact length of frame segment RS.
questions.correct_answer: (a) ΔPQS ≅ ΔRQS by SAS; (b) RS = 12 m
questions.explanation: (a) In ΔPQS and ΔRQS: PQ = RQ = 15 m (Given), ∠PQS = ∠RQS = 35° (Given), and QS = QS (Common side). By SAS criterion, ΔPQS ≅ ΔRQS. (b) Since corresponding parts of congruent triangles (CPCT) are equal, RS = PS = 12 m.
